Function Documentation

int HxPowerEventGetId ( HxPowerMsgData_t *  data  ) 

Retrieves power event identification value.

When an app's receives a power related message, the message contains opaque data structure (should be extracted with HxMessageGetData call) with information about particular power event. Each power event is identified by "power event id" (see HxPowerEvent enum). This function retrieves power event identification value of particular event.

Parameters:
data IN: pointer to opaque type returned by a previous call to HxMessageGetData.
Returns:
int: Returns id of power event attached to the message

int HxPowerEventIsFinal ( HxPowerMsgData_t *  data  ) 

Retrieves "final" attribute of power event.

When system is transitioning to sleep mode a serios of kHxModeSleep events is broadcasted to notify application about mode change. In response to such events application could respond with HxPowerRequestSleepDelay call to buy more time to prepare for sleep. When no more "sleep delays" is requested the system will broadcast final kHxModeSleep event with "Final" atttribute set. This function retrieves the state of "Final" attribute.

Parameters:
data IN: pointer to opaque type returned by a previous call to HxMessageGetData.
Returns:
int: Returns non-zero if "final" attribute of power event is set

HxResult HxPowerEventValidate ( HxPowerMsgData_t *  data,
unsigned int  size 
)

Validates the content of power event received alone with power message.

When an app's receives a power related message, the message contains opaque data structure (should be extracted with HxMessageGetData call) with information about particular power event. This function verifies that received structure contains valid power event.

Parameters:
data IN: pointer to opaque type returned by a previous call to HxMessageGetData.
size IN: size of the data returned by a previous call to HxMessageGetData.
Returns:
HxResult: Returns HX_OK if the content is valid.

HxResult HxPowerRequestSleepDelay ( void   ) 

Delay sleep.

This function will set the sleep countdown timer. In the 'on' state, it will set the timer to the value of 'keepalive_when_on' in powerd configuration file. When not in the 'on' state, it will set the timer to the value of 'keepalive_when_not_on' in powerd configuration file. Calling it repeatedly does not cause the delay time to accumulate.

If the system is currently in 'On' state, the expiration of the sleep timer will send it to the 'Ready' state.

If the system is currently in 'Ready' state (just after power button was pushed or lid closed), the expiration of the sleep timer will send it to the 'WaitSleep' state, where it will send a serios of kHxModeSleep events.

If the system is currently in 'WaitSleep' state, the expiration of the sleep timer will send it to the 'Sleep' state, where all the drivers will receive a HXPM_MODE_SLEEP event and the CPU will then be suspended.

If application needs more time before transitioning into sleep mode, upon receiving kHxModeSleep event an application should respond with HxPowerRequestSleepDelay call to indicate that more time is required. An application should continue responding to each kHxModeSleep event with HxPowerRequestSleepDelay call until it is not ready to transition into sleep mode. An application should be ready to abort transitioning into sleep mode if indicated by kHxModeReady or kHxModeActive events.

Returns:
HxResult: Returns HX_OK if successful.
